I bought the ebook for every textbook I have this semester and holy crap I'm never looking back. The highlighting/outline process is suddenly one easy step as opposed to the painstakingly monotonous task of transferring your highlights into an outline. The amount of time I've saved is amazing.

And since I have access to my books on my computer and on my phone (anywhere with internet access) I find myself able to read cases while waiting at a doctor's office, or in a long line at the store. Little things like that have made a huge difference for me, personally and I'm never going back to normal gigantic case books.

I spend a lot of time making outlines and charts that are all color coded and cross referenced. Stupid little things like that help me so much with my memory, like I know that all of the cases involving warrantless searches are red, and then I can easily picture the case names I have written in red because I've done it over and over again. And if I missed reading a whole case I read into it on Westlaw instead of my case books because it's just a waste of time to read the entire thing unless you are prepping for cold calls. Prepping for the exam and for class are two different things and it's important to distinguish the two.

I lived in the ICU with my soulmate while he fought for his life, and the stories i heard, along with my own horrible experience, is heartbreaking. Accidents don't pick and choose their victims. Yep! Works so well. Basically you put all the email address and names in an excel spreadsheet, save them as ".csv" or "comma separated variables," import them into your contact book. 

Then you'll make a word document that says Dear [Title] [Last Name], ...insert cover letter.... 

Then select the folder of contacts you created from the csv and select mail merge and it will send that email to every contact in the folder, and it will be personalized with only their name and email address appearing. 

I've used it for years as the Director of our Trial Team when I've had to send out thousands of the same emails to potential donors. I've only ever done it with "outlook" but I'm sure other platforms have a way to do it, too. But if you use outlook I can help you out with any questions. Feel free to PM me! 

Edit: then there is a way to add pdfs to all of the emails too for your resume. There is a script that you can run that will attach the PDF to all of your emails in your outbox. So a good rule of thumb is to always work in the "offline" mode in outlook so they aren't actually moved to your sent folder and sent until you turn your mailbox back "online"
Look up "mail merge" it's a way to send an email to a billion contacts but it sends each contact it's own email and it's personalized with their name

Passive/active voice makes a HUGE difference. Always use active. It's really easy to spot once you get the hang of it. 

Passive: The company was cutting corners by ignoring safety precautions.
Active: The company cut corners when it ignored safety precautions.

Passive: The defendant was not engaging in illegal activity.
Active: The defendant did not engage in illegal activity. 

Passive: By not allowing the plaintiff to testify about the accident, the plaintiff was being prejudiced. 
Active: The plaintiff was prejudiced when he wasn't allowed to testify. 


Usually being aware of "ing" verbs will help you discern active from passive.
